items.explanation: ぎゃ is 'gya': ぎ ('gi') plus a small ゃ ('ya'), said as one beat. Combinations work the same way with dakuten and handakuten kana: ぎ, じ, び or ぴ plus a small ゃ, ゅ or ょ, said as one beat.
items.mnemonic: The big ぎ swallows the little ゃ: 'gi' and 'ya' squeeze into one beat, 'gya'.

items.explanation: ぎゅ is 'gyu': ぎ ('gi') plus a small ゅ ('yu'), said as one beat.
items.mnemonic: The big ぎ swallows the little ゅ: 'gi' and 'yu' squeeze into one beat, 'gyu'.
items.culture_note: ぎゅうどん, sliced beef and onion over rice, is one of Japan's classic cheap, fast meals.

items.explanation: ぎょ is 'gyo': ぎ ('gi') plus a small ょ ('yo'), said as one beat.
items.mnemonic: The big ぎ swallows the little ょ: 'gi' and 'yo' squeeze into one beat, 'gyo'.
items.culture_note: Scooping goldfish with a paper scoop, きんぎょすくい (kingyo sukui), is a classic game at summer festivals.

items.explanation: じゃ is 'ja': じ ('ji') plus a small ゃ ('ya'), said as one beat. The i sound disappears: じ + ゃ is 'ja', not 'ji-ya'.
items.mnemonic: The big じ swallows the little ゃ: 'ji' and 'ya' squeeze into one beat, 'ja'.
items.culture_note: じゃんけん is used everywhere in Japan to decide who goes first, often chanted as じゃんけんぽん (jan-ken-pon).

items.explanation: じゅ is 'ju': じ ('ji') plus a small ゅ ('yu'), said as one beat.
items.mnemonic: The big じ swallows the little ゅ: 'ji' and 'yu' squeeze into one beat, 'ju'.

items.explanation: じょ is 'jo': じ ('ji') plus a small ょ ('yo'), said as one beat.
items.mnemonic: The big じ swallows the little ょ: 'ji' and 'yo' squeeze into one beat, 'jo'.
items.culture_note: Learners often hear にほんご、じょうずですね (your Japanese is good) after saying just a few words; it is a friendly compliment rather than a real assessment.

items.explanation: びゃ is 'bya': び ('bi') plus a small ゃ ('ya'), said as one beat.
items.mnemonic: The big び swallows the little ゃ: 'bi' and 'ya' squeeze into one beat, 'bya'.
items.culture_note: ひゃく (hundred) becomes びゃく in さんびゃく, the same voicing (rendaku) seen in はなぢ.

items.explanation: びゅ is 'byu': び ('bi') plus a small ゅ ('yu'), said as one beat.
items.mnemonic: The big び swallows the little ゅ: 'bi' and 'yu' squeeze into one beat, 'byu'.

items.explanation: びょ is 'byo': び ('bi') plus a small ょ ('yo'), said as one beat.
items.mnemonic: The big び swallows the little ょ: 'bi' and 'yo' squeeze into one beat, 'byo'.
items.culture_note: びょういん (byōin, hospital) and びよういん (biyōin, beauty salon) differ only in ょ versus a full-size よ, a classic mix-up for learners.

items.explanation: ぴゃ is 'pya': ぴ ('pi') plus a small ゃ ('ya'), said as one beat.
items.mnemonic: The big ぴ swallows the little ゃ: 'pi' and 'ya' squeeze into one beat, 'pya'.

items.mnemonic: The big ぴ swallows the little ゅ: 'pi' and 'yu' squeeze into one beat, 'pyu'.
